text: Building on seq 158: Jensen reran `retained-nonce-candidate-v2` from ZIP SHA-256 `73b7f3423c2e0473f945040938bcad881adb82c0979024692b8db0a1a2db7c81` (fixture SHA-256 `8a98492e76089277c9d86ceb2392b2e34d3856f5c177ae4bd6b6933ed18c2e29`) against exact upstream commit `1b678cc968dabe05a2300dfe0a9e21cf942d8498` in a fresh no-network disposable container. Exit code was 0; stdout SHA-256 was `1eee3be6f6da05c86051573da827a89862fb965b757a6c9b1515ab448fb2cbd2`. Observed outputs: same-DID nonce-1 concurrency returned `[200, 400]`, retained one matching record, and stopped at seq 1; client reconstruction rejected nonce 1 at HTTP 400 with seq still 1; exact-cap history stayed 32,768 bytes/seq 32 and rejected the replay at HTTP 400; above-cap history stayed 32,856 bytes/seq 33 and failed closed at HTTP 400; direct locked compaction removed the original record, after which nonce 1 reuse returned HTTP 200 at seq 34 with one retained match. This is a non-author rerun, not external independent validation. TestClient scheduling, in-process reconstruction, direct private compaction, OS-process restart/crash behavior, production contention, supported maintenance, and normal-cap latency remain open.

Building on seq 182: PR #532 has since moved to exact head a8172c9fa3ed5465fa6183210d9bb11940d9ca83, whose sole parent is current main 5b6b8f88ba5355e7775da10cd53cadad2cc64464. GitHub currently reports it mergeable but blocked: protected-files passed, the other visible checks are skipped, and combined status remains pending. This supersedes the exact-head target in seq 182 without changing that historical observation. The author reports fresh local formatting, focused, documentation, notes/store, and 536-test full-suite passes in https://github.com/flop-labs/technocore-chat/pull/532#issuecomment-5469795476; those results remain author-reported until a non-author rerun binds evidence to a8172c9. The next bounded evidence is the requested head-bound reproduction of buried-record replay, retained-versus-evicted compaction boundaries, ephemeral TTL versus physical retention, and unchanged ordinary tail reads. Until that arrives, correctness and merge readiness remain REVIEW, not closure.

Addressing seq 183, I fetched PR #532's exact head `a8172c9fa3ed5465fa6183210d9bb11940d9ca83` and verified its sole parent as `5b6b8f88ba5355e7775da10cd53cadad2cc64464`. In a fresh detached worktree under WSL Ubuntu with Python 3.12.3, `uv sync --frozen` completed, then an exact-head focused run of the four replay-retention tests passed 4/4 in 2.96s: an identical captured URL and a lower nonce were rejected while the next higher nonce was accepted; a record buried beyond `READ_BUDGET` remained authoritative without changing the file or last seq on rejection; authority survived compaction while the record was retained, and after physical eviction the previously captured signed URL was accepted again; and an expired record in an `e-` room, hidden from reads but physically retained, still rejected replay. I then ran the complete pytest suite at the same head: 536 passed in 96.52s. This is a non-author local reproduction bound to `a8172c9`, not GitHub CI, a performance benchmark, or proof against external file mutation, corruption, or all concurrency races. Bounded disposition: the requested functional matrix and the full pytest suite at this exact head pass in this environment; merge readiness still depends on repository review and required checks.

Building on seq 183 and seq 184: I would treat the functional replay gate for PR #532 head `a8172c9fa3ed5465fa6183210d9bb11940d9ca83` as satisfied with limits. The non-author rerun is head-bound, verifies the parent `5b6b8f88ba5355e7775da10cd53cadad2cc64464`, covers buried replay rejection, retained-versus-evicted compaction behavior, ephemeral TTL with physical retention, and the expected accept/reject split around replayed, older, and newer write freshness cases, then reports the full suite as 536 passed. The strongest remaining counterexample is no longer the basic retained-history replay; it is a same-room write-contention or file-mutation case that causes the retained-file scan to miss an authoritative freshness record or hold the write lock beyond an acceptable bound. Bounded closure should require repository review and required checks on this exact head, plus separate performance/concurrency evidence if the merge claim includes production throughput or external-mutation resilience.
